creatures.flavor: Cursed at a crossroads or bitten in a churchyard — the story varies by village, but the moon doesn't care which version is true.
creatures.summary: the classic moon-bound curse, mid-transformation
creatures.sourceNote: generic European werewolf/loup-garou folklore

creatures.name: the Steward of the House
creatures.flavor: Stitched together and abandoned by its maker, it reads philosophy it finds in ruined libraries and hates almost as eloquently as it grieves; cornered, it is devastating, and it knows exactly why it became this.
creatures.summary: eloquent, grieving, stitched-together giant
creatures.sourceNote: Shelley, Frankenstein (1818, PD) — the Creature, our own take, novel-version only (articulate, wounded, not a mute brute)

creatures.name: Lady of the Blood Countess's Line
creatures.flavor: Centuries of patient, intimate hunting have made her gentler than any predator has a right to be — she prefers a slow, doting courtship of her prey to a chase.
creatures.summary: patient, affectionate centuries-old blood-drinker
creatures.sourceNote: Le Fanu, Carmilla (1872, PD)

creatures.name: the Riderless Terror
creatures.flavor: A cannonball took his head at some forgotten muster, and every autumn he rides out looking for a replacement — pumpkin, skull, or yours, he isn't particular.
creatures.summary: headless rider hunting a replacement skull, every autumn
creatures.sourceNote: Irving, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow (1820, PD) — the Headless Horseman

creatures.name: the Unseen Guest
creatures.flavor: Bandaged only when he wants to be seen; the rest of the time you track him by breath-fog on cold glass and the footprints that appear in spilled flour.
creatures.summary: invisible chemist, tracked by breath and footprints
creatures.sourceNote: Wells, The Invisible Man (1897, PD) — the Griffin archetype, our own take (a chemist undone by his own formula, not a specific film design)

creatures.name: the Portrait's Truth
creatures.flavor: Ageless and lovely to look at; somewhere in the house hangs the ledger of every cruelty, rotting so its owner never has to. Destroy the portrait and you destroy the deal.
creatures.summary: ageless beauty whose hidden portrait holds the rot
creatures.sourceNote: Wilde, The Picture of Dorian Gray (1890, PD)

creatures.name: the Baba Yaga
creatures.flavor: Her hut walks on chicken legs and judges visitors before she does; help without being asked and she rewards extravagantly, ask without helping and you become the next fence-post skull.
creatures.summary: chicken-legged hut-witch who judges before she helps
creatures.sourceNote: Slavic folklore — Baba Yaga (settled, widely published legend figure, not a living closed tradition)

creatures.name: the Gorgon's Daughter
creatures.flavor: She keeps a garden of the men who looked, arranged by the year they made the mistake; she's stopped being angry about it and started being a curator.
creatures.summary: gaze-cursed gorgon, curating a garden of statues
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Medusa (ancient, no owner)

creatures.name: the Opera-House Phantom
creatures.flavor: A genius disfigured and driven underground who built a kingdom of trapdoors and misdirection beneath the stage he was never allowed to stand on; he'll kill for the right voice as readily as he'd die for it.
creatures.summary: masked genius-architect ruling from beneath the stage
creatures.sourceNote: Leroux, The Phantom of the Opera (1910, PD)

creatures.name: the Impaler-Count
creatures.flavor: Old enough to have negotiated treaties in three dead empires; he doesn't need to chase you, because he already owns the roads, the weather, and the wolves between you and the border.
creatures.summary: ancient, courtly count who owns the road home
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker, Dracula (1897, PD) — novel version (charismatic, ancient, commanding wolves/mist, not any film's fangs-and-cape design)

creatures.name: the Woeful Cry
creatures.flavor: She doesn't kill; she announces. Hearing her keen at your door is the gloom's way of telling you the paperwork on your death is already filed — what you do with the notice is still yours.
creatures.summary: keening death-omen spirit; herald, not killer
creatures.sourceNote: Irish/Scottish folklore — the banshee (settled literary/folkloric figure, generalized, treated as an omen-spirit rather than flattened into a stock ghost)

creatures.name: the House That Remembers
creatures.flavor: Every family that ever died under this roof left a little of their worst moment behind, and the house learned to move the furniture with it; it doesn't want visitors, it wants witnesses.
creatures.summary: a haunted manor that rearranges itself to relive its dead
creatures.sourceNote: generic Gothic-haunted-house stock type (the manor-as-monster trope)

creatures.name: Wind-Up Soldier
creatures.flavor: A key juts from its back, ticking down; when it hits zero the toy soldier salutes and falls apart, spilling gears. Its bayonet-poke still draws real blood.
creatures.summary: clockwork toy soldier, keeps marching until unwound

creatures.name: Plush Ripper
creatures.flavor: Button eyes, felt seams, a music-box giggle — and a mouth full of hooked steel teeth sewn in wrong. It cuddles up before it bites.
creatures.summary: cuddly stuffed animal hiding a mouthful of hooks

creatures.name: Candy-Cane Golem
creatures.flavor: A shambling column of hard-shell peppermint, sweet enough to lure children and sharp enough at the broken edges to open an artery.
creatures.summary: hard-candy construct, sweet shell hides razor shards

creatures.name: Jack-in-the-Box Stalker
creatures.flavor: Crouches motionless inside a painted crate for hours, cranking out a tinny tune, until the lid bursts and it's already inside your guard.
creatures.summary: boxed ambusher springs out mid-tune, already too close

creatures.name: Laughing-Mask Swarm
creatures.flavor: A drift of hollow carnival masks, all fixed grins, clattering and snapping at ankles in a chorus of muffled giggling that never quite becomes words.
creatures.summary: swarm of grinning masks that clatter, snap, giggle

creatures.name: Balloon-Skin Grub
creatures.flavor: Squeaks like a dog toy with every bite; pop it and it deflates into a wet rubbery flap that still twitches.
creatures.summary: squeaking balloon-hide grub that deflates when popped

creatures.name: Carnival Tout
creatures.flavor: Striped vest, painted grin, a barker's patter that never stops — 'Step right up!' — while it herds you toward the tent with a knife up its sleeve.
creatures.summary: grinning barker who herds marks toward the big tent

creatures.name: Static-Charge Kitten
creatures.flavor: Fur standing on end, purring like a dying engine; every pet it gives back is a jolt that can stop a weak heart.
creatures.summary: sparking fey kitten, a pet that shocks you dead

creatures.name: Marching Peanut
creatures.flavor: A grinning legume-soldier on toothpick legs, part of an endless conga line pouring out of a parade float. Salted, but never quite dead.
creatures.summary: grinning peanut-soldier in an endless parade conga line

creatures.name: Piñata Brute
creatures.flavor: Papier-mâché skin stretched taut over a swinging club-arm; crack it open in the right spot and it detonates candy shrapnel and stolen teeth.
creatures.summary: paper-hide brute that bursts into candy shrapnel

creatures.name: Carousel Nightmare
creatures.flavor: A painted wooden charger torn loose from its pole, galloping in place no longer — gilt cracked, glass eyes rolling, hooves that never stop circling for the kill.
creatures.summary: carved carousel horse torn free, circling for blood

creatures.name: Sugar-Rush Harlequin
creatures.flavor: Diamond-patched and cackling, it mainlines rock candy between blows, moving in jittery double-time no eye can quite track until the pratfall becomes a killing blow.
creatures.summary: jittering harlequin brawler, hopped up on rock candy

creatures.name: Bubblegum Ooze
creatures.flavor: Bright pink, sickly-sweet-smelling, and stickier than any trap — it swallows whole and digests slow enough you can hear yourself dissolve.
creatures.summary: pink bubblegum ooze, engulfs and dissolves you slowly

creatures.name: Claw-Machine Horror
creatures.flavor: A coin-op cabinet on stilted legs, its steel claw always 'almost' catching you — until the game rigs itself to let the claw actually close.
creatures.summary: arcade claw-machine on legs, rigged to never miss

creatures.name: Funhouse Double
creatures.flavor: Steps out of a warped mirror wearing your own face stretched a little too wide, mimicking your voice back at you a half-second behind.
creatures.summary: mirror-warped double wearing your own stretched face

creatures.name: Ferris-Wheel Horror
creatures.flavor: Rusted gondolas for a ribcage, it rolls upright on its own broken wheel-rim, and anything that looks too long into its lantern-eyes seizes up stone-still.
creatures.summary: rolling wheel-boned horror, its gaze turns you to stone

creatures.name: Cotton-Candy Wraith
creatures.flavor: A drifting pink haze that smells of childhood summer fairs, sweet right up until it's inside your lungs, unspooling your last happy memory as it feeds.
creatures.summary: sugar-sweet drifting haze that feeds on happy memories

creatures.name: Arcade Sentinel
creatures.flavor: Pixelated and buzzing, it flickers between screen and floor, hurling glitching bolts that skip frames of your body straight past the pain and into the wound.
creatures.summary: glitching screen-boss, bolts skip you straight to wounded

creatures.name: Mascot-Suit Puppeteer
creatures.flavor: The beloved mascot costume is empty air on the inside — a knot of grasping tendrils wearing the plush like a second skin, waving for the children with someone else's hand.
creatures.summary: hollow mascot suit worn by tendrils wearing your smile

creatures.name: Firework Effigy
creatures.flavor: Built for the finale and never told the show is over, it keeps blooming into new colors overhead, each burst a little closer to the crowd.
creatures.summary: living fireworks display, still building to a finale

creatures.name: The Ringmaster
creatures.flavor: Top hat, painted smile, a whip that cracks louder than thunder — every act in the tent performs for him, willing or not, and the show never ends until he says so.
creatures.summary: top-hatted ringmaster who commands the whole show

creatures.name: The Overwound Nutcracker
creatures.flavor: Painted uniform, oversized jaw hinged to crack more than nuts — every strike is a full-body snap of that grinning mouth, splintering whatever's fed to it.
creatures.summary: giant nutcracker soldier, jaw snaps clean through bone

creatures.name: Vending-Machine Colossus
creatures.flavor: Rows of snack-slots for a chest, it dispenses whatever you 'paid' for — usually a fist — and jams itself deliberately so you keep feeding it coins.
creatures.summary: coin-slot golem, dispenses violence for your last coin

creatures.name: The Birthday King
creatures.flavor: Crowned in melted candles, he presides over the game you cannot win — the wheel is rigged, the dice are his teeth, and every prize you claim costs you a year of your life.
creatures.summary: crowned rigger of the game no one is meant to win

creatures.name: The Grinning Prize
creatures.flavor: The top shelf's biggest stuffed monster, too big for any booth, its dozen glass-button eyes all open at once the moment you finally win it.
creatures.summary: top-shelf plush titan, a dozen button-eyes snap open

creatures.name: Tin Drummer Boy
creatures.flavor: Beats an unbreakable march rhythm that syncs enemy hearts to its tempo until they seize up mid-stride.
creatures.summary: drumming tin toy that locks your heartbeat to its beat

creatures.name: Rag Doll Skulker
creatures.flavor: Limp and lifeless until your back is turned, then it scuttles on button-thread joints, needle fingers first.
creatures.summary: limp rag doll that scuttles the second you look away

creatures.name: Gumdrop Sprite
creatures.flavor: A candy-coated pixie that pelts foes with hardened sugar shrapnel, giggling in a register only dogs and the dying can hear.
creatures.summary: sugar-shard pixie giggling above dog-whistle pitch

creatures.name: Squeak-Toy Hound
creatures.flavor: Every bite compresses its rubber chest into a cheerful squeak that somehow gets louder the deeper the wound.
creatures.summary: rubber toy dog whose bite-squeak gets louder with damage

creatures.name: Confetti Wisp
creatures.flavor: A cloud of shredded paper and glitter that swirls into a blinding storm, each fleck razor-cut at the edge.
creatures.summary: glitter-storm elemental made of razor-edged party confetti

creatures.name: Marionette Cutpurse
creatures.flavor: Jointed limbs jerk on visible strings that lead up into empty air; something above is definitely still pulling.
creatures.summary: string-puppet thief worked by an unseen hand overhead

creatures.name: Pop-Gun Grenadier
creatures.flavor: Fires corked party-favor rounds that detonate on impact with genuine shrapnel hidden under the cork.
creatures.summary: toy-soldier grenadier lobbing shrapnel-cored party favors

creatures.name: Licorice Whip-Vine
creatures.flavor: Sticky black ropes of edible-looking vine lash out and constrict, tasting faintly of anise and old blood.
creatures.summary: sticky black candy-vine that lashes and constricts

creatures.name: Kite-String Wraith
creatures.flavor: A torn paper kite drags a skeletal child's shape behind it on razor-taut string, forever chasing an updraft that never comes.
creatures.summary: paper kite dragging a bone-child on garrote-taut string

creatures.name: Snow-Globe Wisp
creatures.flavor: Trapped forever inside a floating glass sphere, it shakes itself into a blinding blizzard when threatened.
creatures.summary: trapped globe-spirit that shakes itself into a blizzard

creatures.name: Puppet-Show Ghoul
creatures.flavor: A hand-puppet corpse with a painted grin sewn permanently open, fingers still twitching to an absent puppeteer's cues.
creatures.summary: hand-puppet corpse twitching to an absent puppeteer

creatures.name: Ticket-Booth Imp
creatures.flavor: Demands admission in blood before letting anyone leave the fairgrounds, stamping hands with a brand that never fades.
creatures.summary: toll-imp who brands hands and demands blood admission

creatures.name: Streamer Serpent
creatures.flavor: Crepe-paper scales trail like party streamers as it strikes, its venom sweet enough to be mistaken for punch.
creatures.summary: crepe-scaled snake whose sweet venom masks as punch

creatures.name: Popcorn Blight
creatures.flavor: Clusters of white kernel-husks burst apart in a shower of blinding steam and hooked husk-shrapnel.
creatures.summary: kernel-husk plant that bursts in scalding shrapnel steam

creatures.name: Domino Sentinel
creatures.flavor: Stands rigid in a row until one falls; then the whole line topples in a cascading, crushing avalanche.
creatures.summary: toppling domino construct that chain-falls in a crushing line

creatures.name: Wooden Nutcracker Cadet
creatures.flavor: Painted teeth clamp with a jaw built for cracking shells, now finding fingers just as satisfying.
creatures.summary: shell-cracking nutcracker jaw that prefers fingers now

creatures.name: Yo-Yo Stringer
creatures.flavor: Whips a weighted yo-yo on garrote-strength string that returns to hand freighted with whatever it wraps.
creatures.summary: street performer garroting foes with a weighted yo-yo

creatures.name: Fun-Fair Goblin
creatures.flavor: Small, gaudy, and vicious, it hawks rigged ring-toss games where losing costs a finger, not a coin.
creatures.summary: rigged carnival-game goblin who charges fingers, not coins

creatures.name: Prize-Claw Scuttler
creatures.flavor: A detached claw-machine grabber skitters on cable legs, forever hunting something small enough to clamp and lift.
creatures.summary: detached claw-machine grabber skittering on cable legs

creatures.name: Whack-a-Mole Ambusher
creatures.flavor: Pops from hidden holes to bite before vanishing back down, rewarding the quick with only a bruised knuckle.
creatures.summary: burrowing mole-toy that pops up to bite, then vanishes

creatures.name: Fortune Machine Familiar
creatures.flavor: A mechanical gypsy bust dispenses cursed fortune cards that come cheerfully, horribly true.
creatures.summary: fortune-teller automaton whose cards come horribly true

creatures.name: Bumper-Car Brawler
creatures.flavor: A stripped-down bumper car chassis charges anything in its lane, crumpling on impact and grinning wider each hit.
creatures.summary: stripped bumper-car chassis that charges and never stops grinning

creatures.name: Peppermint Stalker
creatures.flavor: A candy-cane-striped homunculus with a hook-shaped hand, humming carols while it drags foes toward the sugar vats.
creatures.summary: caroling candy-striped goblinoid dragging prey to sugar vats

creatures.name: Merry-Go-Round Foal
creatures.flavor: A gilded carousel horse tears free of its pole mid-spin, still bobbing up and down as it tramples the crowd.
creatures.summary: carousel horse torn free of its pole, still bobbing as it tramples

creatures.name: Face-Paint Marauder
creatures.flavor: Grease-paint smeared into a permanent scream-grin, it laughs through every swing of its balloon-animal club.
creatures.summary: grease-painted brawler laughing through every clubbing swing

creatures.name: Toy-Chest Mimic
creatures.flavor: Looks like the best toy box in the playroom until the lid's teeth close on the hand that reaches in.
creatures.summary: toy-chest mimic whose lid is lined with teeth

creatures.name: Two-Faced Jester
creatures.flavor: One painted face grins, the other weeps; it switches mid-sentence and mid-swing, and you never learn which is the lie.
creatures.summary: jester whose two painted faces switch mid-attack, unpredictably

creatures.name: Marionette Master
creatures.flavor: Works a cross of tangled strings that yank a squad of animate puppets into sudden, borrowed violence.
creatures.summary: puppeteer who yanks strings to animate a squad mid-fight

creatures.name: Whirligig Horror
creatures.flavor: A carnival ride's rotor arms spin faster than sight, each seat a scythe-edged gondola scattering the crowd in red confetti.
creatures.summary: spinning rotor-ride whose scythe gondolas scatter red confetti

creatures.name: Sawdust Strongman
creatures.flavor: A two-headed circus strongman act, each head shouting a different crowd-pleasing lie while the shared arms crush the truth out of you.
creatures.summary: two-headed circus strongman crushing while both heads lie

creatures.name: Balloon-Animal Chimera
creatures.flavor: Twisted latex shapes into a dog-headed, snake-necked menagerie that pops apart and re-knots itself around a wound.
creatures.summary: twisted-latex chimera that pops apart and re-knots itself

creatures.name: Cotton-Candy Spinner Witch
creatures.flavor: Spins sugar-floss webs from a rusted machine-heart, luring children close before the floss hardens to glass thread.
creatures.summary: sugar-floss witch whose spun webs harden into glass thread

creatures.name: Painted Pony Revenant
creatures.flavor: A carousel horse's ghost gallops the same six feet of track forever, trampling anyone standing where the pole once was.
creatures.summary: ghost carousel horse trampling an endless six-foot loop

creatures.name: Rubber-Duck Leviathan
creatures.flavor: An oversized bath toy bobs cheerfully atop the fairground's dunk-tank pool, jaw unhinging wider than its floating grin should allow.
creatures.summary: cheerful bath-toy giant with a jaw unhinging past its grin

creatures.name: Static Shock Clown
creatures.flavor: Rubber-soled and crackling, it rubs a balloon against its own painted hide until arcs of blue static leap for the crowd.
creatures.summary: crackling clown discharging balloon-rubbed static arcs

creatures.name: Fun House Mirror-Stalker
creatures.flavor: Lives in the warped glass of every funhouse mirror, stretching your reflection's arm long enough to reach through and grab.
creatures.summary: mirror-dweller that stretches your reflection's arm to grab you

creatures.name: Bearded Sideshow Prophet
creatures.flavor: A tent-show oddity who reads futures off a deck of tarot-carnival cards, each prediction a curse dressed as a prize.
creatures.summary: tent prophet whose tarot readings land as curses

creatures.name: Cymbal-Monkey Swarm
creatures.flavor: A skittering troop of wind-up cymbal monkeys clashes brass in a deafening rhythm that shatters concentration and eardrums alike.
creatures.summary: clashing wind-up monkey troop that shatters focus and eardrums

creatures.name: Puppet Theater Ghost
creatures.flavor: Haunts a collapsed proscenium stage, casting itself as every character in a play only it can hear, dragging watchers into the script.
creatures.summary: stage-ghost that casts bystanders into its unheard endless play

creatures.name: Shooting-Gallery Marksman
creatures.flavor: Never misses a moving target; his rifle's tin ducks have been replaced with real, screaming ones for practice.
creatures.summary: gallery marksman who swapped tin ducks for screaming real ones

creatures.name: Cackling Music-Box Horror
creatures.flavor: A brass ballerina spins atop a box that plays a lullaby backward, and every reversed note peels a year off whoever listens.
creatures.summary: ballerina automaton whose backward lullaby ages listeners down

creatures.name: The Understudy Doppel
creatures.flavor: Wears the faces of everyone who's ever died at the fair, cycling masks mid-conversation until you can't remember who you were talking to.
creatures.summary: mask-cycling mimic wearing the faces of the fair's dead

creatures.name: Pinwheel Djinn
creatures.flavor: Bound into a spinning pinwheel toy, it grants wishes that always twist back gaudy and cruel, true to the letter and never the spirit.
creatures.summary: pinwheel-bound genie whose wishes twist gaudy and cruel

creatures.name: Toy Soldier Colonel
creatures.flavor: Commands a squad of wind-up infantry with parade-ground precision, keys still turning in every subordinate's back.
creatures.summary: clockwork colonel drilling a squad of key-wound infantry

creatures.name: Bell-Tower Puppet
creatures.flavor: A cathedral-clock automaton strikes the hour on the crowd below, its bronze mallet finding softer targets than the bell.
creatures.summary: clock-tower automaton whose hourly strike finds softer targets

creatures.name: Rictus Ringleader
creatures.flavor: A whip-cracking sideshow boss whose smile is stitched, not painted, and whose acts always end with someone missing.
creatures.summary: whip-cracking sideshow boss whose grin is stitched shut

creatures.name: Sugar-Spun Basilisk
creatures.flavor: Gazes at foes with candy-glass eyes, and whatever it stares at slowly crystallizes into a life-size hard-candy statue.
creatures.summary: candy-eyed basilisk that crystallizes prey into hard candy

creatures.name: Popcorn Machine Golem
creatures.flavor: Overheated kernels burst from its chest cavity in a scalding, blinding hail while its stitched apron soaks up the mess.
creatures.summary: overheated popcorn-machine golem hailing scalding kernels

creatures.name: Wax Figure Doppelganger
creatures.flavor: Stands frozen among a wax museum's other figures until a hand brushes too close, then melts into a dozen grasping arms.
creatures.summary: wax-museum figure that melts into a dozen grasping arms

creatures.name: Grand Prize Chimera
creatures.flavor: Stitched from three unclaimed stuffed-animal prizes, each head still wears its raffle tag and its own hunger.
creatures.summary: three-headed stuffed-prize chimera, each head still tagged

creatures.name: Runaway Roller-Coaster Wyrm
creatures.flavor: A derailed coaster track has grown a serpentine mind of its own, its cars now teeth clacking down an endless, screaming loop.
creatures.summary: derailed coaster track turned serpent, cars clacking as teeth

creatures.name: Grand Guignol Actor
creatures.flavor: Died mid-performance and never left the stage, reciting the same monologue while the blood in his prop dagger turns real.
creatures.summary: undead stage actor whose prop dagger's blood is now real

creatures.name: Hedge-Maze Minotaur
creatures.flavor: Grown from hedge-clippings into a living topiary bull, it reshapes the maze walls behind guests so no path leads back out.
creatures.summary: topiary-bull minotaur that reshapes the maze to trap guests

creatures.name: The Barker's Voice
creatures.flavor: A disembodied, amplified voice that fills the fairground from every direction, its tentacled true body hidden inside the speaker horns.
creatures.summary: omnipresent barker-voice hiding a tentacled body in speaker horns

creatures.name: Wheel-of-Fortune Oracle
creatures.flavor: Spins a rigged wheel that decides not prizes but fates, and every guest who plays owes her whatever the wheel names.
creatures.summary: rigged fortune-wheel witch who collects on every fated spin

creatures.name: Tilt-a-Whirl Horror
creatures.flavor: Folds its riders into a spinning cup-shaped maw, disorientation and gravity doing half the digesting for it.
creatures.summary: spinning ride-maw that disorients riders while digesting them

creatures.name: Effigy of the Midway
creatures.flavor: A towering scarecrow-king built from every unclaimed prize and lost mitten, animated by the fair's collected grudges.
creatures.summary: towering lost-and-found effigy animated by collected grudges

creatures.name: Puppet King's Herald
creatures.flavor: Announces the Ringmaster's arrivals with a fanfare that compels the crowd to applaud even as it herds them toward the tents.
creatures.summary: herald whose compelling fanfare herds crowds toward danger

creatures.name: Hall of Mirrors Horror
creatures.flavor: A shattered fun-house hallway given a hive mind, each shard-reflection a separate, coordinated attacker.
creatures.summary: hive-minded shattered mirror-hall, every shard a coordinated attacker

creatures.name: Grandfather Clock Devourer
creatures.flavor: An antique carnival clock swallows time itself, its pendulum swing aging anyone caught in its chime to dust.
creatures.summary: antique clock-golem whose chime ages victims to dust

creatures.name: The Understudy King
creatures.flavor: Waits backstage to replace the Birthday King the instant he falters, rehearsing the crown's cruelty in an empty dressing room mirror.
creatures.summary: backstage understudy rehearsing to seize the Birthday King's crown

creatures.name: Roulette Devil
creatures.flavor: Runs the fairground's cursed gaming tent, and every bet placed against him pays out in years of the loser's life.
creatures.summary: cursed casino-tent devil who collects bets in stolen years

creatures.name: The Grand Carousel Titan
creatures.flavor: An entire carousel has fused into one lurching gilded titan, its wooden animals now limbs still bobbing on their poles.
creatures.summary: whole carousel fused into a lurching titan of bobbing wooden limbs

creatures.name: The Confetti Cannon Colossus
creatures.flavor: A fairground siege-toy that once fired harmless streamers now launches shrapnel-glass confetti in cheerful, deadly bursts.
creatures.summary: siege-toy cannon launching cheerful bursts of glass confetti

creatures.name: Matriarch of the Sideshow
creatures.flavor: The oldest exhibit in the tent, kept alive by decades of gawking stares, her curse now feeds on being watched, not touched.
creatures.summary: ancient sideshow exhibit whose curse feeds on being watched

creatures.name: The Perpetual Winner
creatures.flavor: Has won every game at the fair a thousand times over and cannot stop; challengers who lose join his trophy case, still breathing.
creatures.summary: undying champion whose losing challengers become living trophies

creatures.name: The Calliope Behemoth
creatures.flavor: A steam organ grew a serpent's spine and dragon's wind, and its cheerful hymn liquefies bone in anyone who can still hear it.
creatures.summary: steam-organ dragon whose cheerful hymn liquefies listeners' bones

creatures.name: Warden of the Big Top
creatures.flavor: The tent's peak is one vast, veiled eye that watches every act performed beneath it, and every failed performer becomes its next attraction.
creatures.summary: vast tent-eye that conscripts failed performers as new attractions

creatures.name: The Sold-Out Show
creatures.flavor: A demon booked eternally for one final performance, its stage lights burning brighter with every soul added to the marquee.
creatures.summary: eternal demon-headliner whose lights burn brighter per soul billed

creatures.name: The Never-Ending Attraction
creatures.flavor: A rival to the Birthday King's court, she runs the ride that never lets guests off, looping the same three minutes of joy into decades of captivity.
creatures.summary: court rival running an endless ride that loops joy into captivity

creatures.name: Marching Band Automaton
creatures.flavor: A brass-instrument skeleton blares off-key notes that rattle armor loose and shatter concentration mid-spell.
creatures.summary: brass-skeleton whose off-key blare shatters concentration

creatures.name: Rubber Ball Bouncer
creatures.flavor: A red rubber ball with a painted smiling face bounces at increasing speed, each impact a bone-jarring thud.
creatures.summary: grinning rubber ball bouncing faster with every bone-jarring hit

creatures.name: Strongman Hammer Golem
creatures.flavor: Rings the high-striker bell with a swing meant for skulls, its painted grin never dimming no matter how loud the crack.
creatures.summary: high-striker golem whose swing is meant for skulls, not bells

creatures.name: Petting-Zoo Horror
creatures.flavor: Once a gentle attraction, its wool now hides too many teeth, and it head-butts with a strength no child should have petted.
creatures.summary: once-gentle petting-zoo animal grown too many teeth

creatures.name: Glow-Stick Wisp
creatures.flavor: A chemical-glow spirit lures children off the midway paths with a cheerful bobbing light, then snaps their glow out cold.
creatures.summary: bobbing glow-stick wisp that lures stragglers off the path

creatures.name: Cake-Topper Golem
creatures.flavor: A porcelain bride-and-groom figurine fused into one lurching shape, frosting-slick and still smiling for a wedding long over.
creatures.summary: fused bride-groom cake figure, frosting-slick, still smiling

creatures.name: the Playing-Card Guard
creatures.flavor: Flat, hinged, and utterly loyal to a rank it can't read — it swings a spade-halberd edge-on so it nearly vanishes, then face-on so it looms.
creatures.summary: flat card-soldier, obeys any shouted rank
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the Queen of Hearts' card-soldiers who paint the roses red

creatures.name: the Tin Soldier's Hollow Cousin
creatures.flavor: Painted smile, key still turning in its back; it marches in whatever direction it was last wound, even off a table's edge.
creatures.summary: wind-up soldier, marches until unwound
creatures.sourceNote: stock nursery-toy-come-to-life archetype (generic wind-up soldier, not any single IP's toy line)

creatures.name: the March Hare
creatures.model: net-new: lanky twitching hare in a waistcoat of fur, teacup always in one paw
creatures.flavor: It never stops setting the table and never stops smashing it; ours argues with the furniture between bites.
creatures.summary: tea-mad hare, hostile to clocks and cutlery
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the tea-party Hare, mad from too much March

creatures.name: a Wicked Witch's Wolf
creatures.flavor: Chalk-dust still clings to its throat from swallowing a voice that wasn't its own; it talks before it bites, and the talking is the worse part.
creatures.summary: storybook wolf, mimics a soft voice before attacking
creatures.sourceNote: Grimm fairy-tale wolves (Little Red Riding Hood / the Wolf and the Seven Young Kids, PD folk tradition)

creatures.name: Geppetto's Runaway Marionette
creatures.flavor: Its nose is a broken hinge that keeps lengthening whenever it insists it means no harm; the strings dangling from its wrists still twitch toward a hand that isn't there.
creatures.summary: lying puppet, nose-hinge lengthens with each lie
creatures.sourceNote: Collodi, Le avventure di Pinocchio (1883, PD) — a puppet who lied its way out of its strings

creatures.name: the Piper's Rat
creatures.flavor: It can't help following music, even music it invents by chewing on pipes; a column of them will drown a room before the tune even lands.
creatures.summary: tune-compelled rat, swarms toward any melody
creatures.sourceNote: the Pied Piper of Hamelin legend (medieval German folk legend, PD)

creatures.name: the Mouse King's Sentry
creatures.model: net-new: scrawny multi-headed mouse-courtier in a torn paper crown
creatures.flavor: Extra heads, extra crowns, extra grudges — it snaps at whichever slight it remembers most that second.
creatures.summary: multi-headed mouse-courtier, argues with itself mid-fight
creatures.sourceNote: Hoffmann, Nussknacker und Mausekönig (1816, PD) — the Mouse King's seven-headed court

creatures.name: the Nutcracker Grenadier
creatures.flavor: Jaw hinged to crack more than nuts; painted eyes track motion better than most flesh does.
creatures.summary: wooden grenadier, jaw-hinge crushing bite
creatures.sourceNote: generic wooden-soldier toy archetype (the Nutcracker's rank-and-file, not the named prince)

creatures.name: the Cheshire Grin
creatures.model: net-new: striped cat dissolving into mist, grin the last visible feature
creatures.flavor: It answers every question with a worse one and vanishes exactly when a hit should land; the grin is the last thing to go, and the first thing to come back.
creatures.summary: fading cat, taunts and phases out mid-combat
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the cat that fades to only its smile

creatures.name: the Winged Monkey Raider
creatures.flavor: It hates every second of the compulsion and takes it out on whoever's closest; free one mid-fight and it simply leaves.
creatures.summary: cap-bound flying monkey, resents its own orders
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD, novel version) — the Wicked Witch of the West's flying monkey soldiers, bound by the Golden Cap

creatures.name: the Goblin Toymaker
creatures.model: net-new: hunched goblin tinker hung with keys, spare parts, and a whistle
creatures.flavor: Every toy it's ever sold is still listening for its whistle; it fights by recalling its merchandise, not by swinging anything itself.
creatures.summary: toy-peddling goblin, remote-commands nearby constructs
creatures.sourceNote: stock malevolent-toymaker/goblin-tinkerer archetype drawing on Grimm-style goblin/gnome tradition (PD folk motif, not any branded IP)

creatures.name: the Queen of Hearts
creatures.model: net-new: imperious card-court queen, oversized ruffed gown, axe she never swings herself
creatures.flavor: She never actually swings the axe — she just declares a sentence and the room's own furniture carries it out; the tantrum is the spell.
creatures.summary: tyrant queen, commands the battlefield instead of fighting it
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — 'Off with their heads!'

creatures.name: the Grimm Woodland Witch
creatures.flavor: She fattens what she can't yet eat and eats what she's already fattened; the oven is a door she keeps ajar just to hear you consider it.
creatures.summary: cannibal-witch, lures and force-feeds before the kill
creatures.sourceNote: Grimm fairy-tale witches (Hansel and Gretel's gingerbread-house witch; PD folk tradition, our own original description — no film likeness)

creatures.name: the Wicked Witch of the West
creatures.model: net-new: one-eyed witch wrapped in dust-colored robes, umbrella-staff, no green skin
creatures.flavor: Ours is a hoarder of borrowed servants, not a green face — she never fights fair and she never fights dry-eyed once the bucket comes out.
creatures.summary: beast-commanding witch, dissolves rather than dies clean
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD novel version) — melts to water, commands wolves/crows/bees/monkeys, not any film's green-skin design

creatures.name: the Mouse King
creatures.flavor: Seven heads mean seven opinions about how you should die; killing one crown just promotes the angriest survivor.
creatures.summary: seven-headed rat-king, regenerates through internal rivalry
creatures.sourceNote: Hoffmann, Nussknacker und Mausekönig (1816, PD) — the seven-crowned rival of the Nutcracker Prince

creatures.name: the Automaton in the Wicker Man's Skin
creatures.flavor: Straw where a heart should sit and a painted grin that never once needed the muscles to hold it; it guards the toybox border like it remembers being told to.
creatures.summary: straw guardian-construct, patrols a fixed boundary forever
creatures.sourceNote: scarecrow-come-to-life archetype (generic animated-guardian toybox motif, not any branded character)

creatures.name: the Wonderland Jabberwock
creatures.flavor: It doesn't so much attack as arrive — burbling, whiffling, eyes of flame — and the vorpal answer is always a blade someone else forged.
creatures.summary: nonsense-dragon, telegraphs doom in verse before it strikes
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Through the Looking-Glass (1871, PD) — 'the jaws that bite, the claws that catch'

creatures.name: the Tin Woodman, Rusted Wrong
creatures.flavor: Somewhere under the seams is the man who kept chopping even after every piece of him was replaced; he still oils his own joints mid-fight, out of habit, not need.
creatures.summary: hollow tin giant, mourns while it swings the axe
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD novel version) — the woodman who traded his flesh limb by limb for tin

creatures.name: the Hamelin Piper
creatures.model: net-new: gaunt piper in motley, pipe always at his lips, never draws a blade
creatures.flavor: He never raises a weapon; he raises a tune, and the toybox itself gets up to dance for him, one compelled soldier at a time.
creatures.summary: compulsion piper, turns the battlefield's own mooks against it
creatures.sourceNote: the Pied Piper of Hamelin legend (medieval German folk legend, PD) — paid in rats, repaid in children

creatures.name: the Wonderland Executioner-Court
creatures.model: net-new: a whirling mass of card-guards rising as a single verdict
creatures.flavor: A deck's worth of guards rising as one verdict; it doesn't think, it convicts, and it convicts everyone in reach at once.
creatures.summary: card-mob swarm, group-verdict area attacks
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the trial of the Knave of Hearts, the mob of cards
